text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, just a day after coming through open heart surgery, sent Bill Clinton a message of congratulations on his reelection to the White House on Wednesday.
"In the name of the Russian leadership and for myself personally, I congratulate you on your election," Yeltsin said in a statement released by the Kremlin press service.
"We are ready to continue intensive contacts with your administration in accordance with the current agenda," the Russian leader told the man he likes to call "my friend Bill".

"In recent years, acting in concert, Russia and the U.S. have created a basis for the development of a relationship of constructive and equal partnership. Russia is interested in such relations with the U.S. and considers them as essential conditions for world security and stability," he added.
"We think our work together will be fruitful and will allow us to agree on mutually acceptable decisions that meet the interests of both our countries and the whole world community."
Clinton had wished Yeltsin a speedy recovery before he underwent multiple heart bypass surgery on Tuesday. Doctors said on Wednesday they were pleased with Yeltsin's progress.
Analysts said Moscow favoured the prospect of continuity in Washington over a victory for Republican challenger Bob Dole.

But independent foreign policy experts said the two former Cold War foes now face a testing period in which difficult problems, swept under the carpet as both Yeltsin and Clinton sought re-election this year, finally have to be tackled.
